summary: Microsoft/Bing is Riverside's most cost-efficient paid channel by a wide margin - blended CPA $7.41 vs Google $44 - yet it receives only 1.2% of total ad spend ($43K of $3.69M over 90 days). Brand campaigns are exceptional: US brand $2.43 CPA on $7,401 spend (22,497 clicks at $0.33 CPC), WW brand $3.61 CPA on $5,408 spend. The generic podcast campaign (bing_search_us_desktop_generic_podcast_exact) is the structural weakness: $19,585 spend at $29.41 CPA with $9.56 CPC, inflated by broad audience at exact match type. Two zero-conversion keywords ('software for podcast recording' $50, 'descript for podcasting' $50) are negative keyword candidates. The campaign's naming convention and structure are clean. The dominant finding is severe underfunding relative to demonstrated efficiency - Microsoft guidance recommends 20-30% of Google search budget; actual allocation is ~1.3% of Google total, representing the largest recoverable efficiency gap in Riverside's paid portfolio. Creative, technical setup (UET/Enhanced Conv), LinkedIn targeting enablement, and extension utilization cannot be assessed via Windsor and require manual verification.

findings.title: Microsoft Ads critically underfunded - 10x below minimum recommended allocation
findings.evidence: Bing spend: $43,051 (90 days). Google total: $3,444,660 (1.25% ratio). Google search alone: $2,394,530. Microsoft guidance: Bing = 20-30% of Google. Minimum recommended Bing budget: $478,906/90 days. Actual: $43,051 - 9% of minimum. Bing CPA: $7.41. Google estimated CPA: ~$44. The channel delivers 5.9x more conversions per dollar spent.
findings.remediation: Increase Bing budget incrementally using the 20% Rule: first increase to $60K/90 days, evaluate CPA stability over 2 weeks, then escalate toward $120K, $200K, $400K in stages. Fund increases by reallocating from Google campaigns with CPA >3x target (especially Google Video $115/conv and Google PMax $65/conv). Monitor Bing CPA for diminishing returns signals - the channel likely saturates before $400K but has significant headroom.
findings.est_impact: Scaling Bing from $43K to $200K over 90 days (using $7.41 CPA) projects ~21,000 additional conversions vs ~3,500 from equivalent Google spend at $44 CPA. Net conversion uplift: 17,500 incremental conversions for same $157K reallocation.

findings.title: Generic podcast campaign CPC $9.56 - above Google benchmark, no CPC advantage visible
findings.evidence: bing_search_us_desktop_generic_podcast_exact: $19,585 spend, CPC $9.56, CPA $29.41. Expected Bing CPC for B2B SaaS: $3.50-6.00 (20-35% below Google $4.50-8.00). At $9.56 CPC this campaign is likely overbidding or hitting audience saturation on Bing's smaller inventory. It is also the largest single Bing campaign (45.5% of Bing spend).
findings.remediation: Review bid strategy and target CPC in Microsoft Ads UI. Check for bid adjustments inflating CPCs (device, location, audience). Run a search term report - 'podcast' broad intent on Bing may be attracting high-competition consumer searches. Add negative keywords for non-commercial intent (e.g., 'free', 'how to', 'what is'). Consider splitting into tighter ad groups by intent tier.
findings.est_impact: Reducing CPC from $9.56 to $6.00 on this campaign would save ~$7,300 at current conversion volumes, or yield 40% more clicks for the same budget.

findings.title: Two zero-conversion keywords ($50+ spend each) - negative keyword candidates
findings.evidence: 'software for podcast recording' (bing_search_us_desktop_generic_podcast_exact): $50.63 spend, 3 clicks, 0 conversions. 'descript for podcasting' (bing_search_en_desktop_competitors_presence): $50.18 spend, 8 clicks, 0 conversions. Additionally, 'using zoom to record a podcast': $61.56 spend, 2 conversions, CPA $30.78 (approaching 3x if target CPA is ~$10). 'best video podcast platform': $59.90, 0.36 conversions - near-zero.
findings.remediation: Add 'software for podcast recording' and 'descript for podcasting' as exact-match negative keywords to their respective campaigns immediately. Review 'using zoom to record a podcast' and 'best video podcast platform' for pause if CPA continues above 3x target over next 30 days.
findings.est_impact: Immediate removal of $100+ wasted spend. More importantly, establishes discipline of weekly negative keyword review as Bing budget scales up - critical hygiene at higher spend levels.

findings.title: LinkedIn profile targeting status unverified - high-value B2B differentiator
findings.evidence: LinkedIn profile targeting on Microsoft Ads delivers 16% greater CTR and 64% greater CVR than non-audience-targeted ads. CPCs are 30-70% cheaper than LinkedIn direct. This is especially relevant for Riverside.fm's SLG enterprise segment targeting podcast creators, marketers, and media producers - all job functions available in Microsoft's LinkedIn audience dimensions (148 industries, 26 job functions, 80,000+ companies).
findings.remediation: In Microsoft Ads, navigate to campaign > Audiences > Add audience > LinkedIn Profile. Apply to brand and competitor campaigns in Observation mode first (bid-only, no exclusion). Monitor CTR and CVR lift over 2 weeks. If lift confirmed, apply to generic podcast campaigns in Targeting mode.
findings.est_impact: 64% CVR improvement on B2B-targeted Microsoft campaigns could reduce CPA from $7.41 to $4.52 on targeted segments - further improving already best-in-portfolio efficiency.

findings.title: Brand campaign syndication control unverified - Critical budget waste risk
findings.evidence: bing_search_us_desktop_brand_exact ($7,401) and bing_search_ww_desktop_brand_exact ($5,408) are Riverside's lowest CPA campaigns ($2.43 and $3.61). If these are running on the Microsoft Audience Network or low-quality syndicated partners without exclusions, brand CPA will inflate and impression quality will drop. Windsor cannot confirm partner network settings.
findings.remediation: In Microsoft Ads, check campaign settings > Networks for both brand campaigns. Ensure 'Microsoft sites, apps, and select traffic' only (exclude Audience Network). Run a Publisher URL report for syndicated partners and exclude any site with >$5 spend and 0 conversions.
findings.est_impact: Protects $12,809 of brand campaign spend from quality degradation. Brand campaigns are the highest-ROAS campaigns in the account - preserving their efficiency is critical.

findings.title: Audience Network status unverified - B2B CPA risk if enabled
findings.evidence: Microsoft Audience Network is enabled by default on all campaigns. B2B advertisers (Seer Interactive data) see CPA 2-4x higher from Audience Network than search alone. Riverside.fm is B2B SaaS. If Audience Network is ON across all 9 campaigns, it is likely inflating CPAs on generic and competitor campaigns.
findings.remediation: Check each campaign's network settings. For performance campaigns (competitors, generic), disable Audience Network. If Audience Network is enabled for testing, set a separate campaign to isolate its performance, run publisher URL reports weekly, and build an exclusion list.
findings.est_impact: Disabling Audience Network on non-brand campaigns could reduce CPA by 50-75% on affected campaigns by eliminating low-quality traffic.

findings.title: Conversion goal validation post-import required
findings.evidence: Windsor uses conversions_qualified (legacy field), which works but is deprecated. The note confirms standard 'conversions' field returns 0 in Windsor, suggesting a UET / conversion goal configuration that may rely on the legacy event type. If campaigns were imported from Google Ads, conversion goals are a known break point - imported goals often stop firing.
findings.remediation: In Microsoft Ads UI, verify each conversion action under Tools > Conversion Tracking. Confirm goals are firing, match expected values, and are assigned to the correct campaigns. Validate with a test conversion if in doubt. Deactivate any scheduled Google Ads imports to prevent goal overwriting.
findings.est_impact: If conversion tracking is partially broken, optimization signals are degraded and Smart Bidding algorithms may be underbidding on high-converting queries.

findings.title: Action Extension not confirmed - Microsoft-unique CTA format
findings.evidence: Action Extensions are exclusive to Microsoft Ads (not available on Google) and add predefined clickable CTA buttons to ads. Cannot verify current usage via Windsor. For Riverside.fm, relevant actions include 'Sign Up', 'Get Started', and 'Try for Free'.
findings.remediation: In Microsoft Ads, check Extensions > Action Extensions per campaign. Add Action Extension with 'Sign Up' or 'Get Started' CTA to all search campaigns. 5-minute setup.
findings.est_impact: Extension adoption typically improves CTR 10-15% by increasing ad real estate and clarity of CTA.

findings.title: Copilot placement not applicable - evaluate PMax addition for Copilot CTR lift
findings.evidence: No Performance Max campaigns in current Bing account. Copilot chat placements (73% CTR lift, 16% CVR lift) are primarily available through PMax and Multimedia Ads. As Bing budget scales, PMax would unlock Copilot inventory.
findings.remediation: As part of the Bing budget scaling roadmap, create a Microsoft Ads Performance Max campaign targeting trial signups. Enable Copilot placement in PMax settings. Evaluate Copilot Checkout (Jan 2026) for PLG trial conversion flow.
findings.est_impact: Copilot placement delivers 73% CTR lift and 194% purchase intent increase. At Riverside's SaaS funnel, this could meaningfully reduce CPA below the already-excellent $7.41 blended.

findings.title: UET tag installation and firing rate requires manual verification
findings.evidence: Windsor provides campaign metrics only. Universal Event Tracking (UET) tag status, firing rate, and page coverage cannot be confirmed. Without a fully firing UET tag, conversion data is incomplete and Smart Bidding algorithms are operating on partial signal.
findings.remediation: Install Microsoft Clarity + UET Helper extension. In Microsoft Ads, check Tools > UET Tag and verify 'Active' status and no error flags. Confirm firing on homepage, pricing, trial start, and post-signup pages.
findings.est_impact: Foundation for all Microsoft Ads optimization. Required before scaling budget.

findings.title: Scheduled Google Ads import status unknown - risk of silent campaign re-enablement
findings.evidence: Windsor cannot reveal whether scheduled auto-imports are active. Scheduled imports are a common source of billing surprises: they can re-enable paused campaigns, overwrite manual bid/budget changes, and reset conversion goals. This risk scales significantly if Bing budget is increased.
findings.remediation: In Microsoft Ads, navigate to Import > Google Ads Import > Scheduled Imports. Disable any active scheduled imports. Switch to manual import-on-demand only. Document which campaigns were imported vs created natively.
findings.est_impact: Prevents unexpected spend events as budget scales. Particularly important before implementing the recommended budget increase.
